one_month_reasoning: One stock-specific event is in the window: Q3 2026 results after the close on 2026-10-20 [19][30]. Consensus is about $2.91B revenue and $2.64 non-GAAP EPS [19], and management guided to near the 14.5% midpoint of 13.5-15.5% da Vinci procedure growth [1]. Base rates point slightly up. In my own daily data, the Q3 report day was positive in all seven years from 2019 to 2025 (+7.0, +1.6, +1.0, +9.0, +0.1, +10.0, +13.9%) [27]. The 4-week return from the first week of October was positive in 10 of 16 years since 2010, with a median of about +6% [28]. Against that, 2026 reactions have been large and two-sided: -14.1% on 2026-07-17 after a beat, and +7.2% in April that was fully given back within a month [27]. Recent volatility is also high: 3-month realized is 49% (inflated by the July gap) against 37% over 1 year [27]. Two macro events also fall in the window. The FOMC meets on Oct 27-28: after the September 16 hike, Kalshi priced 65% hold and 33% hike on Sep 30 [21], down from about 66% hike a week earlier, so October is less hawkish than I had assumed. The 10-year yield, however, is at 5.29% and rising [24]. Short interest is low at 2.3% of float, so there is no squeeze fuel [31]. A Section 232 device-tariff proclamation remains possible at any time [16][36]. I centre the month at about $405 (+1%, a slight tilt from the Q3 and October base rates) with roughly 11.2% one-month volatility (37%/3.5 = 10.6%, bumped for the earnings event) and t(5) tails.

fair_value.method: A blend of four methods: forward P/E (NTM non-GAAP EPS ~$13.0 at Oct-2027 x 33x = $429, weight 0.40), EV/EBITDA (NTM EBITDA $6.49B x 21x + ~$10.6B net cash over 355M shares = $414, weight 0.30), trailing GAAP P/E (FY2027 GAAP EPS $10.02 x 42x = $421, weight 0.15) and an own-history base-rate drift (+10% = $441, weight 0.15). The blend comes to about $425.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: NTM non-GAAP EPS at Oct-2027 ~$13.0 x 33x forward P/E

inputs_detail.derivation: $12.09 x 1.13. Bloomberg consensus EBITDA grows 14.1% from FY2027 ($5.87B) to FY2028 ($6.70B) [25]. I take slightly less for EPS, as procedure growth decelerates.
0.25 x $12.09 + 0.75 x $13.66 = $13.27, cut to $13.0 for revision risk: soft US elective volumes (HCA Q2 surgeries down 2-3% [35]), Ottava/Hugo pricing pressure [32][34] and tariffs [16].

Today's price is about 34x NTM non-GAAP EPS ($401.24 / (0.25 x $10.78 + 0.75 x $12.09 = $11.76)) [2]. Medtech peers trade at about 15-22x and the sector median NTM P/E is about 16x against a 25x five-year median [26][25]. The 10-year yield is 5.29% [24]. I assume no re-rating and a slight drift down as EPS growth decelerates from ~21% (2026) to ~12% (2027).

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.inputs: NTM EBITDA at Oct-2027 $6.49B x 21x = EV $136.3B; + net cash ~$10.6B; / 355M diluted shares

Market cap $141.75B [29] less $8.63B cash and investments [1] gives EV $133.1B; divided by $5.87B.
Slight compression from 22.7x. Peer EV/FY2027 EBITDA: SYK 16.2x, EW 18.2x, BSX 13.9x, PEN 33.7x [25]. ISRG's faster growth justifies a premium, but rising long rates [24] argue against expansion.
$8.63B at Q2 2026 (no debt) [1], plus ~5 quarters of FCF at $3.2B TTM [29] (~$4B), less ~$2B of buybacks at the Q2 pace of ~$0.4B/qtr [1].
353.3M outstanding [29]; Q2 diluted count ~357M; buybacks roughly offset dilution.

methods.name: other
methods.inputs: Trailing GAAP P/E: FY2027 GAAP EPS $10.02 x 42x

inputs_detail.derivation: Barchart's consensus ($8.87 for 2026 and $10.02 for 2027) is on a GAAP basis, consistent with Q2 GAAP $2.29 vs non-GAAP $2.80 [1].

Today's trailing GAAP P/E is 46.6x [29] and the 10-year range is 33.5-93.6x on the same GAAP basis [6]. If the stock were flat, ~15% trailing EPS growth would take the multiple to ~40x; 42x allows modest support near the historical low end. Correction from round 1: I had applied this GAAP P/E range to non-GAAP EPS.
Own computation on weekly closes. The 2025 episode was the exception: median -10%.

I shrink the +23-28% history hard toward a market-like return. It is survivorship-biased (ISRG was a 50-bagger), the latest analog (2025) was negative, and the sector-wide medtech de-rating [26] and recovery times averaging ~25 months [37] argue for patience.

bear.story: US procedure growth guided to 10-12% for 2027 in January as weak elective volumes (HCA surgeries down 2-3% in Q2 [35]) and GLP-1 effects on bariatrics persist [38]. Ottava and Hugo general-surgery wins [32][34] force price concessions, and a Section 232 device tariff [16][36] cuts gross margin. Long rates keep climbing past 5.3% [24]. Estimates fall to ~$12.3 NTM and the stock de-rates to ~24-25x, toward the medtech peer group [25][26]. This resembles 2013, when growth slowed and the stock took about a year to bottom [10][11].

base.story: Procedure growth runs around 13-14%, dV5 placements and trade-ins stay strong (246 dV5 of 468 placements in Q2) [1], and Ottava stays capacity-limited through 2027 [32]. EPS tracks consensus ($12.09 for 2027) [2], and the multiple holds at ~33x NTM EPS of ~$13. That is about +7%.

bull.story: Competitive fears fade (Oppenheimer calls US competition a non-factor near term [32]; JPM surgeon checks show no share loss [4]). Procedure growth re-accelerates as GLP-1 and ACA headwinds lap, and rates roll over. The stock repeats its 2022-23 and Dexcom-2024 style recoveries [28][12][13], re-rating to ~42-43x NTM EPS of $13.3, near the upper analyst targets ($483 median, $685 high) [2][3].

thesis_break_reason: $300 is about 9% below the 2026 low of $328.57 and implies ~23x NTM non-GAAP EPS (~30x GAAP), under the 10-year GAAP trailing P/E floor of 33.5x [6] even on today's earnings. A trade there would most likely mean estimates themselves are being cut: visible share loss to Ottava or Hugo, 2027 procedure growth guided below ~11%, or a material device tariff or pricing reset. It would not be ordinary 34-37% volatility around a de-rated but intact franchise. Even the deepest 12-month outcome after a comparable drawdown since 2010 was -18% [28], which from here would be about $330.

Whether US elective volumes recover in 2027 after ACA-subsidy disenrollment (HCA surgeries down 2-3% in Q2 2026)

Small and clustered base-rate sample: ~7 independent drawdown episodes since 2010, and the most recent (2025) was followed by a further decline
reasoning: This continuation adds about 25 searches and fetches, mostly in the base-rates lane. (1) Own-history base rates, rebuilt on weekly data since 2000 [28]. Since 2010, after 25-42% drawdowns from the 52-week high, the median 12-month return was +28% with only 9% negative, but that is 100 overlapping observations from ~7 episodes. The latest episode (spring 2025) was followed by a median -10%, so the pattern is weakening. Unconditional 12-month returns since 2010 have a median of +23%, a 10th percentile of -20% and are negative 25% of the time; weekly realized vol since 2010 is 31% (33% over 5 years). (2) Macro has turned more hostile than I knew in round 1. The Fed hiked on Sep 16, the 10-year is at 5.29% (a multi-decade high for the 30-year) [24], Polymarket prices ~81% odds of another 2026 hike [22], and recession odds are only ~8.5% [23]. Medtech as a whole has de-rated to ~16x NTM, a 30% discount to the S&P [26], with BSX, PODD and others down 20-38% [25]. Much of ISRG's de-rating is therefore sector and rate driven, not company-specific, and that argues against assuming the multiple snaps back. (3) Competition is real but slow. Ottava launches with select customers under limited production capacity, and Oppenheimer sees US competition as a near-term non-factor (~15% J&J share by 2030) [32][33]. Hugo's general-surgery 510(k) is pending [34]. (4) Fundamentals are intact: Q2 revenue +19%, da Vinci procedures +15%, 468 placements and raised gross-margin guidance [1]. Consensus is unchanged at $10.78/$12.09 [2]. (5) One correction from round 1: my trailing-P/E method applied a GAAP P/E range (33.5-93.6x) to non-GAAP EPS. Redone on GAAP EPS ($10.02 for 2027 [19]), it gives $421, not $435. Adding an EV/EBITDA method ($414) and a shrunk base-rate drift ($441) brings fair value to $425, down from $440. Scenarios are $300/$430/$570 at 25/50/25% (mean ~$432). The ladder uses a t(5) log distribution with median $421 (+5%) and 34% vol (between the 31-33% long-run and 37% 1-year realized; the 49% 3-month figure is inflated by the July gap). That gives P(>= $401) = 0.57, P(>= $321) = 0.83 and P(>= $602) = 0.12. Analyst targets ($476 average, $483 median [2]) remain above my median; I treat them as evidence of sentiment, not the answer. Remaining limits: Alpha Vantage was rate-limited, CNBC and some prediction-market pages blocked fetching (used syndicated or summary copies), and there is still no prediction market on device tariffs or on ISRG itself.
